To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the metabolic stability of DNA in liver is related to the level of gene expression, and that DNA condensates cross-linked to a high-mannosylated glycopeptide with poly(ethylene glycols) can be targeted to Kupffer cells in liver.
the metabolic stability of cross-linked DNA co-condensate formulations in liver can be manipulated to control the duration and level of gene delivery in vivo.

the metabolic stability of DNA co-condensed with low molecular weight glycoconjugates is dependent on the cross-linking density, and that this parameter influences the level of gene expression in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new class of glycoconjugate-mediated gene delivery system that is capable of specifically targeting DNA to Kupffer cells, which is a major barrier to the systemic delivery of DNA to peripheral tissues.
the development of a novel approach to target therapeutic genes to specific cell types in vivo by using glycopeptide-mediated DNA condensates.

the design and development of a new type of DNA carrier system, termed cross-linked glycopeptide-mediated DNA condensates, that can target DNA to the liver and mediate sustained gene expression in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolic stability of DNA in liver is the primary factor that determines the level of transient human alpha1-anti-trypsin expression.
the level of transient transgene expression is dependent on the metabolic stability of DNA co-condensed with glycopeptide-peptide conjugates and cross-linked with glutaraldehyde.

the level of gene expression in vivo is dependent on the metabolic stability of DNA in liver, and the level of gene delivery can be optimized by controlling the formulation parameters of cross-linked DNA co-condensate formulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA metabolic stability in liver is a major determinant of the level of gene expression in vivo and can be manipulated through the judicious choice of DNA condensation agents.

the use of cross-linked glycopeptide DNA co-condensate formulations for in vivo gene delivery is a viable strategy for targeting DNA to Kupffer cells in liver, which is mediated by a receptor-mediated endocytosis mechanism.
cross-linking DNA co-condensate formulations can be used to increase the metabolic stability of DNA and to control the level of gene expression by altering the rate of DNA clearance from liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the metabolic stability of DNA co-condensed with glycopeptide/PEG-peptide cross-linked with glutaraldehyde is a function of the cross-linking density, which can be manipulated to achieve the desired level of gene expression in vivo.
the level of transient expression of therapeutic proteins in vivo can be controlled by modulating the metabolic stability of DNA in liver.
the stability of the DNA condensate in vivo, which is determined by its crosslinking density, is an important determinant of the level of transgene expression in vivo.
